owner_statement:
Withdraw 4 ms p95 / 8 ms p99 as blocking criteria because their derivation was never validated. Preserve historical measurements and all correctness obligations.

Establish a measured reference baseline from a stable, pinned candidate on the reference host, using representative workloads, verified input/output, complete timing boundaries, and measured instrumentation effects. Reuse adequate existing evidence; collect only what is missing. Report per-trial p95/p99, sample counts, variability, configuration, and limitations. Do not select only favorable runs.

Keep baseline and acceptance budget distinct. The baseline describes observed performance; it does not automatically define acceptable performance. Propose replacement budgets using the measured distributions, demonstrated responsiveness, supported hardware expectations, and an explicit rationale for any headroom or required improvement.

Obtain owner approval of that rationale before making replacement budgets blocking. If the evidence cannot support a defensible number, leave it explicitly undecided; do not invent one to complete the specification.

Apply this precedent to future numerical performance requirements: every binding threshold must cite its derivation, supporting evidence, applicable configurations, and review conditions. Audit adjacent CPU, GPU-duty, and resource thresholds for unsupported assumptions without silently changing them.

Amend the controlling specifications, roadmap, and agent handoff together so functionality development can proceed while this bounded baseline-and-budget work is scheduled explicitly.
scope: GPU frame 4 ms p95 and 8 ms p99 withdrawal; governance/roadmap reconciliation; scheduled gap-only baseline and budget work. CPU 4/8 ms is a distinct adjacent requirement audited without change. All correctness remains.
